summary: Both recordings create a can of grease but do not apply it. After the apply command, key o selects BLINDFOLD (object type 233); the earlier inventory screen lists the can of grease at p. C therefore reaches apply.c doapply()’s BLINDFOLD/LENSES switch arm and calls Blindf_on(), while JS has no matching dispatch and stops in its default unsupported arm. This is the first stop at segment 0 step 17; the missing source owner is the eyewear arm in doapply(), not use_grease().

source.branch: After getobj() returns a BLINDFOLD or LENSES object that passed apply_ok(), if the selected object is not already ublindf and ublindf is empty, doapply() calls Blindf_on(obj). These recordings enter that branch with the initial blindfold unworn. If the selected item is already ublindf, C may call Blindf_off() unless cursed; if other eyewear is worn, C prints the already-covered message. Those sibling branches are not reached.
callers: C cmd.c command table binds key a to doapply(); doapply() calls getobj("use or apply", apply_ok, GETOBJ_NOFLAGS) before its object-type switch.
JS cmd.js runApplyCommand() calls doapply(state) for the apply command. The stop is in js/apply.js doapply() after its switch lacks BLINDFOLD/LENSES cases.
dependencies: C apply.c apply_ok() suggests TOOL_CLASS objects, and apply.c doapply() obtains the selected item through getobj(); the recorded item key o selects the blindfold, while the preceding screen identifies the can of grease as p.

C doapply() calls do_wear.c Blindf_on() for the unworn-eyewear branch. Blindf_on() removes a worn-item mask if needed, sets the object in W_TOOL (ublindf), calls on_msg(), and toggles blindness when the hero becomes blind; its void return is ignored and doapply() keeps its initial ECMD_TIME result.

The common C do_wear.c Blindf_on() path is already implemented in js/do_wear.js Blindf_on(); the current first stop is before that helper because js/apply.js doapply() has no BLINDFOLD/LENSES dispatch case.

evidence: The saved evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260926132731-v6.json reports 17/19 screens, 2361/2366 RNG calls, and 17/19 cursors matched. Its first stop is segment 0 step 17 on key o: JS reports the missing doapply() arm for object type 233.

The C recording challenges/cases/v6/wizard-grease-hands-good.session.json has seed 60626051 and moves Ctrl-W, can of grease, then ao-. At step 15 the C screen says “p - a can of grease.”; step 16 starts the apply prompt; key o at step 17 produces “You are now wearing a blindfold. You can't see any more.” and status Blind. This evidence rules out the can-of-grease arm as the first divergent branch.

C nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:4150-4212 defines apply_ok() and begins doapply(); apply_ok() suggests TOOL_CLASS objects for getobj(). The BLINDFOLD/LENSES branch at apply.c:4244-4257 calls Blindf_on(obj) when obj != ublindf and ublindf is empty. apply.c:4282 handles CAN_OF_GREASE separately, after the eyewear arm.

C nethack-c/upstream/src/do_wear.c:1461-1492 owns the common sighted-to-blind transition: Blindf_on() sets W_TOOL, calls on_msg(), detects the blindness transition, then calls toggle_blindness(). JS already implements this common path in js/do_wear.js:1042-1098; js/apply.js:2297-2403 lacks BLINDFOLD/LENSES cases, so execution reaches the unsupported default instead.
